title: A Stitch in Time Saves… Ten Later
text: Time to confirm whether Panda was at the tavern in question, I say. She wasn’t inside, so Father and the others took seats to wait. Just like last time, Elephant went off with Father, Panda’s foster father, and grandfather to have a word with the tavern master, and they all sat down. When we suggested bringing Older Sister along as well, she seemed eager to come, but this time she said she’d stay behind to mind the house.
“Waah!”
Filo-tan was gazing all around at the unfamiliar sights of Siltvelt, indeed.
“Fu fu fu, ain’t she somethin’.”
Panda’s foster father watched Filo-tan with a warm, indulgent expression.
“Where in the world has Lars run off to this time. Honestly…”
“Now, now, don’t say that. The girl’s got mercenary work to tend to, ain’t nothin’ to be done about it.”
“Still… well, I suppose that’s fair.”
Apparently Panda’s grandfather had once worked as a mercenary himself, back in the day. Otherwise, so the story goes, he never would have met Granny during the war.
“Um, so, Elmelo says this dish here is supposed to be really good—”
Kou, who’d come along with Elephant, was trying to introduce Filo-tan to the tavern’s signature dish.
“Which is tastier, this or Master’s cooking?”
“Iwatani and the others’ cooking is way better!”
“Oh, is that so.”

Such was the exchange between Kou and Filo-tan. That wretch Rafumi once had the nerve to claim that Filo-tan and Kou were barely distinguishable apart from gender—a remark deeply insulting to both parties, I say. Where, pray tell, is the resemblance in their appearances?
“Fu fu, and what does Shield Hero-sama think about fine cuisine?”

Watching Filo-tan and the others chatting away, Panda’s foster father turned to ask Father. Father answered honestly that he found it delicious. When Father was in a bad mood, apparently, he just ate in silence. Incidentally, on this particular topic, it seems the shared worry among Father and his companions was that people kept mistaking them for gourmets and getting intimidated by it.
“Seasoning preferences change depending on the region, so I think it really comes down to the individual. It’s more about how well you can match what the other person likes.”
“Hoh… and judging by that seasoning, it’s clear you don’t just talk about it—you actually put it into practice, indeed.”
“Well… I’m sure there are people out there who believe there’s some universal, perfect dish that works for everyone, though.”
“Indeed there are. Plenty of folk in Zeltoble still cling to that notion, in fact. Speaking of which, wasn’t there some trouble over in Lute Village?”
“Ah, yes, there was. They were having some kind of trouble at the inn I was staying at, so I gave them some advice.”
So it seemed the request that had come to Panda’s foster father had, just as I’d predicted, already been resolved by Father. Truly, Father never disappoints, I say.
“Even so, there’s still a lot about the flavors of this world I don’t fully understand, so adapting to each place is tricky.”
“That’s somethin’ you just pick up as you go, ain’t it.”
“I know full well you lot have been messing around with my preferred seasoning lately for fun. Don’t go doing anything weird, you hear?”
“What’s weird about it? We’re just seein’ how far we can push things to suit a person’s taste, that’s all.”
“It’s good practice, figuring out how much variety you can get out of just bamboo grass as a theme. So, what does Larsazusa-san like?”
“Ah, that girl—used to be fond of stir-fries and steamed buns, back in the day.”
While we were chatting away like that, Elephant came back.
“No luck again this time?”
“No, she’s already returned, so she should be arriving any moment now—”

Just as she said that, the tavern door creaked open, and in walked Panda. Her eyes landed first on Elephant inside the tavern. Then she looked at me, and her brow furrowed. Well come, indeed, Panda. Since Older Sister is rather shy about these things, someone needs to properly keep Father company, I say.
“Oi, over here, I say!”

So I raised my hand and called out to her, and Panda turned her head toward her foster father and grandfather, seated on either side of Father—then her eyes went wide, and she spun on her heel, apparently trying to march straight back out of the tavern.
“Sis? What’s the matter?”
“Turning around all sudden like that.”
“I just remembered I had somethin’ to take care of, that’s all!”
She looked for all the world like she was about to bolt like a startled rabbit, but surely that was just my imagination, I say.
“Panda, we’ve been waiting for you, indeed.”
“Lars, it’s been a while. Come on over here.”
“You came all this way. Sit down.”

At the sound of mine, the foster father’s, and the grandfather’s voices, Panda’s attempt to flee visibly stalled, and with a creak—slowly, reluctantly—she turned back around and came over. Then she marched right up to me and grabbed me by the collar.
“Oi! You! What grudge do you have against me to pull something like this!?”
“Lars, ain’t that a bit rough?”
“How uncouth… perhaps I should have taught her a bit more refinement.”
The grandfather muttered this while sipping the tea that had just been brought over. Panda shot him a wary glance before turning to look at Elephant.
“Oi! Elmelo! What is the meaning of this!”

“Your defeat came down to two mistakes. First, you didn’t come along with us from the start. Second, you stayed away for far too long. Give it up, Lars, there’s no escaping this. Just hearing them out… will do the least damage.”
Elephant pressed her palms together as if praying for Panda’s courage, then glanced toward Father.
“Tch.”
Panda sat down in her chair, looking thoroughly displeased. It was only then that she seemed to finally notice Father, blinking at him with a somewhat puzzled expression.
“I never did explain last time, did I. This is Father, indeed. So do listen properly to what he has to say, I say.”
“Ah? You’re the protection target this guy asked me to guard?”

“Um, nice to meet you, Larsazusa-san. My name’s Naofumi Iwatani. Elmelo-san already gave me a rundown of whatever introduction Motoyasu-kun gave you, and I’ve also heard about it from your foster father and grandfather.”
“Hah… geez, you sure look young for your age.”
“No, I’m… actually twenty.”
“Ahh!?”
Panda glared daggers at me.
“I suppose if all you heard was the job description, that misunderstanding makes sense. Lars, we made sure to get the full picture on our end before coming to invite you like this.”
Elephant added, filling in the gaps for Panda.
“Why…”

Panda swept her gaze from Elephant, then to her foster father, then to her grandfather. Father seemed to have caught on as well—apparently the grudge Panda held wasn’t against him specifically, but against the fact that her foster father and grandfather were both here together.
“I felt bad about it, but there was nothing else to be done. Your hometown village turned out to be a real comfortable place to live, and everyone’s grateful for it.”
“Hold on! What’s that supposed to mean!”
Panda rounded on her foster father and grandfather in turn, voicing her protest to each.
“A noble and worthy cause, that.”
“It was an interesting proposal. That’s all there was to it.”

At their replies, Panda looked as if her head were spinning, sinking deep into her chair and hanging her head. For some reason, she gave off the aura of despair of a boxer who’d just lost a match. The foster father, upon learning of Big Sister and the others’ circumstances, had decided to lend his support, while the grandfather had been throwing himself daily into his ongoing rivalry with Granny. And of course, he was putting just as much effort into the circus performances too.
“I don’t really get what’s goin’ on, but… ain’t this guy over here kin of yours, sis?”
“Idiot, obviously he’s a blood relative and someone she can’t lift her head to, no matter how you look at it.”
Panda’s subordinates seemed thoroughly confused.
“What’s going on here? Oi.”
One of the subordinates looked over at Father.
“Ahaha…”
“…Somehow, like… could it be…”
Panda’s underlings, looking at Father, seemed to be picking up on something.
“You lot shut it and go drink over there.”
Panda, looking utterly resigned, lifted her head and began ordering drinks. Drowning her sorrows, was she?
“Well… I can’t deny that this might, in some small part, be my own curiosity that dragged everyone into this. So… sorry about that.”
